solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/global-and-local-inversions/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

775. Global and Local Inversions

You are given an integer array nums of length n which represents a permutation of all the integers in the range [0, n - 1].

The number of global inversions is the number of the different pairs (i, j) where:
- 0 <= i < j < n
- nums[i] > nums[j]

The number of local inversions is the number of indices i where:
- 0 <= i < n - 1
- nums[i] > nums[i + 1]

Return true if the number of global inversions is equal to the number of local inversions.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,0,2]
Output: true
Explanation: There is 1 global inversion and 1 local inversion.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1,2,0]
Output: false
Explanation: There are 2 global inversions and 1 local inversion.

Constraints:

    n == nums.length
    1 <= n <= 10^5
    0 <= nums[i] < n
    All the integers of nums are unique.
    nums is a permutation of all the numbers in the range [0, n - 1].
"""


class Solution:
    def isIdealPermutation(self, nums: List[int]) -> bool:
        # The number of global inversions equals the number of local inversions
        # if and only if there is no global inversion that is not local.
        # A global inversion that is not local means there exists i < j with j > i+1 and nums[i] > nums[j].
        # So we check if any element is more than 1 position away from its sorted position.
        for i, num in enumerate(nums):
            if abs(num - i) > 1:
                return False
        return True


sol = Solution()

print(sol.isIdealPermutation([1, 0, 2]))  # True

assert sol.isIdealPermutation([1, 0, 2]) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([1, 2, 0]) == False

assert sol.isIdealPermutation([0]) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([1, 0]) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([1, 0, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([0, 2, 1, 3, 4, 5]) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([2, 1, 0, 3, 4, 5]) == False
assert sol.isIdealPermutation(list(range(100000))) == True
assert sol.isIdealPermutation(list(range(99998)) + [99999, 99997]) == False
assert sol.isIdealPermutation(list(range(99997)) + [99999, 99998, 99996]) == False
assert (
    sol.isIdealPermutation([i if i % 2 == 0 else i - 1 for i in range(100000)]) == True
)
assert (
    sol.isIdealPermutation([i if i % 2 == 1 else i + 1 for i in range(100000)]) == True
)
assert sol.isIdealPermutation([99999] + list(range(99999))) == False
